brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A small-leaf kuding from Yuqing County, Guizhou, made from young shoots of a privet of the olive family. It differs entirely from the large-leaf holly kuding of Guangdong, Hainan and Guangxi.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Originally gathered wild, it was first produced as samples in 1994 and planted at scale from 1997. A local standard followed in the early 2000s, and in 2004 sales collapsed after an adulteration scandal around another region's kuding. It gained geographical indication protection on 25 August 2005 and a Panama exposition gold award in April 2013.
processing: Only whole young shoot tips are picked and tightly finished.
harvest_season: Picking begins around Lichun, the start of spring, and earlier picks are prized.
appearance_wet: Vivid emerald; dry leaf, liquor and spent leaf are all green, the so-called three greens.
taste_profile: Clean aroma with a fresh, sweet taste, and a marked bitterness from its phenolic acids.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
